Issue no. 2 Whether the petitioner is entitled to any compensation, if so, to what extent and from whom?

OPP.
13.
As discussed in issue no.1, petitioner is entitled to compensation.

Since it stands proved that the accident occurred due to rashness and negligence of Respondent no.1 as already discussed in issue no.1, Respondents no.2 and 3 are vicariously liable to compensate the petitioner.
Further, as offending vehicle is not insured, liability to compensate the petitioner falls upon all the Respondents jointly and severally.

The court or the Tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable.

Accident occurred on 19.04.2019.
As such, petitioner would have been about 26 years at the time of accident.

As per MLC Ex.PW-1/2, injured Amar Singh suffered laceration on left side of scalp, temporal region above the ear, abrasion in the right elbow, abrasion in the right shoulder with swelling and tenderness and abrasion in the left knee.
As per the MLC, the opinion on the nature of injury was reserved as the petitioner was under observation.
Another document showing further detailed diagnosis at the same hospital reveals mild head injury with multiple contusions in brain.
This document discloses that the X-ray and radiological investigation were prescribed, however, no subsequent document regarding diagnosis on such investigations have been filed.
Keeping in view the nature of injuries particularly sustained in the vital region i.e. the head, the injury can be assumed to be grievous in nature.

However, as no medical bills have been filed on record, noting that the petitioner went for treatment in respect of severe MACT NO:992/19 Amar Singh v. Vijender @ Kale P.No. 10 Of 19 BK head injury, at a renowned private hospital, it is ass
As regards loss of earning of the petitioner, it first needs to be ascertained as to what was the nature of job and salary/wages drawn by petitioner at the time of accident.
Petitioner has claimed to be doing work of catering and earning Rs.18,000/- p.m., however no evidence has been lead to prove his employment or salary.

As petitioner has neither placed any record of his educational qualification or proof of employment, his monthly income is taken on the basis of minimum wages of un- skilled labour of Delhi of the year 2019 is taken.
Same is Rs.14,468/-.
Having regard to the documents on record and the nature of injury suffered, it is assumed that the petitioner may have been incapacitated from working for at least three months.
Accordingly, petitioner is entitled to compensation towards loss of income for three months.
As such, loss of income would have been taken as Rs.14,468/-X3=Rs.43,404/-, accordingly granted.
He is also entitled to attendant charges for the said period.
No compensation towards future loss of income can be granted in cases where petitioner has not proved to have sustained any permanent disability.
